label: no
controls_available: Difficulty 3 uses a 9x8 isometric course with a five-stroke hand: roll 2 east, roll 1 south, chip 1 east, chip 2 south, and roll 2 east before the generated board transform and card shuffle; the route has one sand landing, three water hazards, two ramps, twelve decoy tiles, and chip clearance of two height levels.

Full interaction is a mouse pointer drag: drag any unused pictured stroke card directly onto one of the north, east, south, or west compass targets and release it there. A valid stroke synchronously moves the ball and spends that card.

The screenshot shows the course canvas, ball, cup, tile surfaces, elevations, ramp arrows, and the visible card hand. The CERTIFY SUNKEN BALL button submits the replay after all strokes; certification is administrative.

The environment metadata declares mouse and keyboard, but this mechanic installs no keyboard handler. In full mode a card click or compass click alone does not dispatch a stroke; only the card-to-compass drag does.
autonomous_processes: None affects the course outcome between agent actions. Generation creates the course, ball start, cup, and shuffled cards as fixed state; it contains no timer, motion, physics, or future state transition.

Between strokes the browser mechanic has no interval, timeout, animation-frame loop, or polling loop. A stroke calls transition, updates the ball and used-card set, redraws, and updates status synchronously inside the pointerup handler.

The CSS hover and drag effects are presentation transitions only; they are caused by pointer state and do not change course geometry, ball legality, or card value. The certification fetch happens only after an explicit administrative submit action.

clause_i.reason: For the outcome-affecting drag mode, prior actions and task times alone cannot select the optimal next card and direction across generated instances: the visible transform, shuffled hand, tile surfaces, heights, ramps, and hazards vary while the same empty or prior-action history can occur. The current screenshot is needed to plan the static route.

clause_ii.reason: The current screenshot contains the complete relevant course and hand, and the state does not evolve while waiting. Thus a bounded stationary visual policy with w=0 can choose the same card and direction that would remain optimal after any hypothetical positive delay inside the task opportunity. No consecutive-frame evidence is needed.

clause_iii.reason: There is no positive-delay interval in which the environment autonomously changes the task state while success remains possible. Waiting leaves the course, ball, unused cards, and stroke legality unchanged; only a dispatched stroke changes them. Any loss caused solely by exceeding the 180-second allowance would be clock/deadline loss, which the definition excludes. Therefore no available action has the required strict Q loss or Q-advantage loss from non-clock state evolution.

common_visible_process: No common visible autonomous process exists. The static isometric board and card hand provide the information for planning, but no visible motion, trajectory, phase, or other task-state evolution occurs between actions; consequently no legitimate D, Delta>0, and bounded w can witness all three clauses.

pre_run.reason: The mathematical definition already fails at clause (iii), so the pre-run threshold cannot change this configuration-level No. The source has no autonomous outcome phase to evaluate.

source_evidence.claim: The exact level-3 profile is the five-stroke 9x8 course with one sand route index, three water tiles, two ramps, twelve decoys, and chip clearance two; full mode is direct card drag to a labelled compass, and the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame.
The runtime also declares a zero-ms observation window, one frame per observation, and a 180-second play allowance; these settings do not add mechanic state evolution.
Controlled conditions are normalized and passed into the generator, and cloudstep_caddie is dispatched to the incubator generator rather than a different legacy mechanic.

The level-3 route/profile is static; generation applies the requested difficulty condition, constructs fixed tiles/cards/solution, and only randomizes the generated initial course, transform, palette, and card order.
The generated public state exposes the fixed course and hand while ground truth stores the corresponding static replay solution and control condition.
Full mode makes cards draggable, accepts pointerup only when dropped on a compass direction, and synchronously records the stroke then updates ball position, spent cards, readout, and canvas.
Status and certification are event-driven; full-mode compass clicks only display an instruction, and render performs an initial hand/compass/canvas draw without installing a task-time loop.
The only relevant card motion is a short hover/drag presentation transition; the CSS does not animate or mutate the course state.
Grading independently replays the ordered stroke transcript against the fixed public course and checks exact card use and cup position; it reads no elapsed time or autonomous trajectory.
The verifier loads the exported result and Cloudstep Caddie grader, then grades the submitted replay; it does not introduce a time-dependent mechanic.
The full solver performs the same direct card-to-compass drag sequence from the stored solution and only waits 120 ms between synchronous strokes; that solver-side wait is not task-state evolution.

The frozen definition requires one common visibly evidenced autonomous process that makes an action strictly worse during Delta, and excludes deadline-only loss, static puzzles, and information that remains actionable indefinitely.
